ui.endTitle: A delivery he does not want
ui.endText: Behind him, Cinderfold is cold for the first time in Mara's life. In his satchel, the regulator pulses against his hip, slow and steady, like something waiting for an answer.

line.nothingSpecial: Nothing I haven't seen a thousand times.
line.gauntletLook: Mum's design, my repairs. With the ember cell in, it hums like a cat by a stove.
line.notebookLook: Half diagrams, half unfinished sentences. She always meant to come back to them.
line.notebookLookAfter: The release order is on page forty. Her handwriting gets smaller when she was worried.
line.regulatorItemLook: It's still warm. It pulses every few breaths, as if it's listening for something. The kiln is cold… so what is it answering?
line.breadLook: Still a little warm. Nell wrapped it in her second-best cloth.
line.scarfLook: Tobi's scarf. It smells of hearth smoke and boiled sweets.
line.breadEat: Not yet. It's for the road.
line.scarfWear: I'll wear it once I'm out of sight. Tobi would never let me hear the end of it.
line.heroUseItem: I'd rather keep it in the satchel.
line.heroLook: Courier, door-fixer, kiln-minder. Whatever needs doing today.
line.heroLookCold: I don't feel like a hero. I feel like the person who switched off the heat.
line.heroTalk: Talking to myself again. Nell says that's how it starts.
line.heroLie: Very convincing. Nobody will ask me to carry anything now.
line.rackLook: The charging rack. Mum built it for the gauntlet's ember cell.
line.rackLookEmpty: An empty rack. It looks wrong without the cell glowing in it.
line.rackEmpty: The cell's already in the gauntlet.
line.rackTake: The cell clicks into place. The gauntlet wakes up, warm and humming. Right, what needs fixing today?
line.notebookOnBench: Mum's notebook, on the workbench where I left it. Open at the page about latch springs.
line.notebookOpen: Valve sketches, pressure tables… and a note in the margin: "ask Oren about the ring."
line.notebookTake: I'll take it. I always end up needing a page I didn't think I'd need.
line.nicheLook: The kiln mouths glow through the hall. I fall asleep to that light every night.
line.nicheLookCold: Dark. I have never seen the kiln mouths dark.
line.nicheUse: I warm my hands. Old habit.
line.nicheUseCold: Nothing to warm my hands on.
line.roomCurtainLook: The way down to the firing house, and probably soup.
line.latchAlreadyFixed: It's already working. I'd only make it worse.
line.maraLatch: It sticks when the room cools. I'll check it again tomorrow.
line.maraNightShift: Save some for the night shift.
line.latchLook: Nell's pantry door. The latch hangs crooked again.
line.latchLookFixed: Straight and polished. It'll hold until the next cold snap.
line.latchOpenFixed: It opens. It closes. Nell will be thrilled.
line.latchStuck: Stuck tight. The gauntlet could ease the spring, but not while its cell is still on the rack.
line.latchStuckHint: Bare hands won't do it. The gauntlet can ease the spring.
line.soupBread: Bread and soup, the two pillars of Cinderfold. But this bread is for the road.
line.soupLook: Onion soup. Nell says the secret is patience. I suspect the secret is onions.
line.soupLookCold: The pot is wrapped in blankets to keep the last of the heat in.
line.soupTake: Nell would chase me with the ladle.
line.soupUse: I stir it once, for luck. Nell pretends not to see.
line.shoesLook: Rows of children's shoes, warming for the night. Half of them are Tobi's, somehow.
line.shoesLookCold: The shoes are cooling on their racks. Someone has started taking them down.
line.shoesTake: I'd never hear the end of it.
line.hearthLook: The hearth draws its heat from the kiln. Everything here does.
line.hearthLookCold: The hearth is dark. I did that.
line.hearthUse: I hold my hands to the hearth. It's the warmest place in the village.
line.stairsLook: The stairs up to the regulator gallery. Oren's domain.
line.stairsNotYet: Oren doesn't like visitors while he's reading the gauges. I'll wait until he calls.
line.gateLook: The kiln gate. Beyond it, the ashways and everything that isn't home.
line.gateLookReady: The ashways are on the other side. The First Hearth is somewhere beyond them.
line.gateNotYet: I've got no reason to go out there. Everything I care about is in here.
line.gateLeave: Deliver it. Get an answer. Come back.
line.toRoomLook: The way back to my room.
line.regulatorGone: There's nothing left to do there. It's in my satchel.
line.maraPatch: The patch should hold. It held last winter.
line.orenLockingRing: The crack has reached the locking ring, Mara.
line.notReady: Not yet. I need to talk to Oren first.
line.needProcedure: Mum wrote down the release order. I'm not guessing with this.
line.releaseOne: Outer bolts. Pressure down. Ring a quarter turn… now.
line.orenShelter: We'll arrange shelter. Go on. The First Hearth will know what to do.
line.maraPulse: Oren… the kiln's cold. Why is it still pulsing?
line.notebookTooSoon: Maybe it won't come to that. Let me try the patch first.
line.notebookNotReady: I'm not ready to read that page yet.
line.procedureAlready: I know the order now. Outer bolts, pressure, ring.
line.notebookProcedure1: "Outer bolts first. Bleed the pressure. Only then the ring, a quarter turn and never more."
line.regulatorLook: The kiln's regulator. A crack runs through the casing like a frown.
line.regulatorLookRing: The crack has reached the locking ring. Patches won't hold it now.
line.regulatorLookCold: An empty socket. The gallery is already cooling.
line.regulatorBareHands: Not with bare hands. Not this.
line.gaugeLook: The needle shivers near the red. It sounds like a cough that won't clear.
line.gaugeLookCold: The needle has dropped to zero.
line.gaugeUse: Tapping it won't change what it says.
line.logbookLook: Oren's logbook. Pressure readings, each one worse than the last.
line.logbookTake: Oren would notice before I reached the stairs.
line.lanternLook: The gallery lantern. It's always lit. Oren says the dark makes the machines nervous.
line.galleryStairsLook: The stairs down to the firing house.
line.sweeperFight: I only need a way through. I'm not going to fight something that's just doing its job.
line.sweeperRegulator: When the regulator pulses, the sweeper shivers… then turns back to its pipe.
line.sweeperLookPipe: It's tending the pipe as if nothing else in the world matters.
line.sweeperLook1: An ash sweeper. It turned its brushes toward me… and then turned back.
line.sweeperLook2: It's ignoring me. It's circling that pipe like it's guarding it.
line.sweeperTalk: Excuse me? …No. It doesn't do conversation.
line.sweeperUse: I'd rather not get my fingers anywhere near those brushes.
line.valveAlready: It's still hissing. That'll keep the sweeper busy.
line.valveVented: It cares more about that pipe than about me. Good to know.
line.valveLook: A steam valve on the old pipe. Rusted, but the wheel still turns.
line.valveLookVented: Steam pours out of the valve. The sweeper fusses over it.
line.valveClose: I'd rather leave it open until I'm through.
line.passageLook: The passage under the bridge. The sweeper is right in the way.
line.passageBlocked: Not with that sweeper in the way.
line.farewell: To the First Hearth, then. And back. I'm coming back.
line.pipesLook: The old pipes carry heat between the kilns. Some of them still feel warm.
line.pipesUse: I press a hand to the pipe. It's warm. Warmer than it should be.
line.wayBackGo: Not until I've delivered it. They're counting on me.
line.orenItem: Keep your things, Mara. You'll need them more than I do.
line.orenLook: Oren. He's tended the kiln since before I was born. His hands shake, but he can hear a fault in the pipes.
line.orenLookCold: Oren's already making a list of who sleeps where.
line.orenLookDown: Oren, lying on the gallery floor with perfect dignity.
line.orenCrouch: My knees remember the old furnace. They're not fond of it.
line.orenLie: If it makes you feel better.
line.orenStand: Enough nonsense. There's work to do.
line.nellItem: I've got enough clutter in my pantry, thank you.
line.nellLook: Nell. She runs the soup pot, the gossip and half the village. She carries the old counter shutter around like a shield. Draughts, she says.
line.nellLookCold: Nell is counting blankets out loud, very firmly.
line.nellLookDown: Nell is lying very still, but she's still holding the ladle.
line.nellCrouch: I'm only doing this because my bad hip can't hear you.
line.nellLie: Wake me when the soup's done.
line.askCrouch.oren: Oren, could you crouch for a moment?
line.askCrouch.nell: Nell, could you crouch down for me?
line.askLie.nell: Nell, could you lie down for a moment?
dlg.oren.before1: The gauge sounds wrong today. Like a cough that won't clear.
dlg.oren.before2: If you've got a patch in that gauntlet of yours, now's the time.
dlg.oren.argue1: You heard it, Mara. It's not going to hold. If it bursts, we lose the rooms too.
dlg.choice.repair: There has to be another repair.
dlg.choice.mother: My mother built half of this.
dlg.choice.leaving: I don't want to leave while everyone's packing blankets.
dlg.choice.whyMe: Why does it always have to be me?
dlg.oren.repair1: You've kept it alive three winters with patches and stubbornness. I watched every one.
dlg.oren.repair2: This time the crack is in the ring itself. I won't pretend otherwise. Not to you.
dlg.oren.mother1: I know. Her handwriting is on every valve tag in this gallery.
dlg.oren.mother2: Taking it out doesn't undo her work. It might be how we keep it.
dlg.oren.leaving1: You're scared for them. So am I.
dlg.oren.leaving2: Nell will run the shelter in the lower rooms. You won't be leaving them alone. You'll be leaving them with each other.
dlg.oren.whyMe1: Because you're the only one trained on the locking assembly. That isn't fair, and I'm sorry it's true.
dlg.oren.whyMe2: I'm asking, Mara. Not ordering. I need you to hear the difference.
dlg.hero.decide2: Because if it bursts, everyone here gets hurt.
dlg.oren.decide3: We'll arrange shelter. Can you take the regulator for assessment?
dlg.hero.decide4: To the First Hearth. And then I'm coming back.
dlg.oren.decide5: Your mother wrote down the release order. Read it before you touch the ring.
dlg.oren.minute: Take it. Just not too long. The needle isn't waiting.
dlg.oren.notebookFirst: Notebook first. Then the gauntlet. In that order.
dlg.oren.ready: Let the gauntlet take the pressure, not your arm. And breathe.
dlg.oren.cold1: We'll manage. The shelter's set and the night shift has blankets.
dlg.oren.cold2: Go to the First Hearth. Come back and tell us what they said.
dlg.choice.stillWarm: Oren… it's still warm. It's pulsing.
dlg.oren.stillWarm1: Regulators hold their heat for a while.
dlg.oren.back: I know. Now go, before I start saying sentimental things.
dlg.nell.first1: Mara! My latch is sulking again.
dlg.nell.first2: It sticks every time the room cools. Which is always, lately.
dlg.nell.again: Still stuck. I've started climbing in through the window. Don't tell Tobi.
dlg.nell.noise: Oren shouted. Oren never shouts. Go on, I'll keep a bowl back for you.
dlg.nell.later: Not too much later. The soup won't wait and neither will I.
dlg.nell.cold2: Don't look at me like that. You did the right thing, even if it feels like the wrong one.
dlg.nell.cold3: Here. Bread from this morning, while it still remembers the oven.
dlg.nell.coldAgain: Go on. We'll keep each other warm. We always have.
line.pulleysLook: The pulley hoist. It lifts the clay jars to the upper racks, and squeaks in two keys.
line.pulleysUse: I give the rope a tug. It squeaks in the second key.
line.jarsLook: Storage jars. Half are clay, half are cracked, all of them are Nell's, somehow.
line.jarsTake: Nell counts them. She would know.
line.cartLook: An ash cart. Full, as always.
line.cartUse: I'm not pushing that. Not today.
dlg.nell.cold4: And Tobi left this on the hearth for you. He says it's still warm, so you have to take it.
line.tentFlapLook: The tent flap. Warm light from the kiln hall leaks through, like every morning.
line.tentNotYet: Not without the gauntlet working. The cell is still on the charging rack.
line.workbenchLook: My workbench. Gloves, a bowl of dried apricots, and three repairs I promised for yesterday.
line.workbenchUse: Later. The latch springs can wait one more hour. Probably.
line.jarLook: Drinking water. I fill it at the cistern every second day, when I remember.
line.jarTake: It's heavier than it looks, and it looks heavy.
line.stoolLook: A three-legged stool with four legs. I fixed it twice.
line.stoolUse: If I sit down now, I will start reading the notebook and never leave.
line.drumLook: An old brush drum from a sweeper. I'm keeping it for parts. That's what I tell Nell.
line.drumUse: I give it a spin. It squeals, then sulks.
line.toTentLook: My tent, pitched against the hall wall. Small, warm, mine.

obj.notebook: Take Mum's notebook. I always end up needing it.
obj.latch: Fix Nell's sticking latch in the firing house.
obj.oren: Go up to the gallery and see why Oren called.
obj.procedure: Find the release order in Mum's notebook.
obj.leave: Leave Cinderfold through the kiln gate.
obj.sweeper: Find a way past the ash sweeper.

hint.cell.1: The gauntlet is dead weight without its ember cell. Where does the cell sleep at night?
hint.cell.2: Pick up the ember cell from the charging rack in the tent.
hint.notebook.1: I never go anywhere without Mum's notebook. It should be somewhere in the tent.
hint.notebook.2: Pick up the notebook lying open on the workbench in the tent.
hint.latch.1: Nell's latch only sulks when it's cold. Bare hands won't ease that spring.
hint.latch.2: In the firing house, use the pressure gauntlet on Nell's pantry door.
hint.oren.1: Oren called from up in the gallery. Whatever it is, he expects the gauntlet to fix it.
hint.oren.2: Climb the stairs in the firing house, then use the gauntlet on the regulator to patch it.
hint.talk.1: Oren wants an answer. He'll wait while I say what's on my mind.
hint.talk.2: Talk to Oren and choose at least two of the worries before saying "All right. I'll do it."
hint.procedure.1: Mum wrote down how to take the regulator out. I shouldn't guess.
hint.procedure.2: Use Mum's notebook on the regulator to read the release order.
hint.release.1: I know the order now. Outer bolts, pressure, ring. The gauntlet takes the strain.
hint.release.2: Use the pressure gauntlet on the regulator.
hint.leave.1: The First Hearth is beyond the ashways. The way out is through the kiln gate.
hint.leave.2: Go down to the firing house and go through the kiln gate.
hint.sweeper.1: The sweeper cares about that old pipe more than about me. Can I give it something to fuss over?
hint.sweeper.2: Use the pressure gauntlet on the steam valve, then take the passage under the bridge.
line.rackLook.2: Mum built the cradle from an old lantern frame. She said a cell sleeps better if it can see itself glow.
line.rackLook.3: The cell hums at a pitch only the gauntlet and the dog two tents over can hear.
line.notebookOnBench.2: There's a pressed fern between the pages about valve seats. I've never asked where it came from.
line.notebookOnBench.3: The cover is held together by stitching, glue and habit.
line.jarLook.2: There's a chip on the rim exactly where my thumb goes. It was there before me.
line.jarLook.3: Cistern water tastes faintly of clay. Nell says that's how you know it's from home.
line.workbenchLook.2: Every scratch on this bench is a repair. Some of them even worked.
line.workbenchLook.3: The apricots are for emergencies. Everything is an emergency by noon.
line.stoolLook.2: The fourth leg is a pipe offcut. It's the only one that doesn't wobble.
line.stoolLook.3: Tobi says it's a throne. Tobi says a lot of things.
line.drumLook.2: The bristles are still black with somebody else's ash.
line.drumLook.3: One day it'll be a fan. Or a mill. Or still a drum.
line.tentFlapLook.2: I patched the flap with a flour sack. You can still read "FINEST" if the light's behind it.
line.tentFlapLook.3: The hall's warmth breathes in around the edges, like it's checking on me.
line.toTentLook.2: The canvas has gone the colour of toast from years of kiln light.
line.toTentLook.3: Every tent in the hall leans toward the kiln, like plants toward a window. Mine leans furthest.
line.nicheLook.2: Each mouth has a name chalked over it. The middle one is "Grandmother." Nobody remembers why.
line.nicheLook.3: You can tell the hour by the colour: orange at night, yellow when the morning shift stokes it.
line.pulleysLook.2: I oiled it last month. It squeaks out of loyalty now.
line.pulleysLook.3: The rope has three knots where three people swore it would never fray again. One of them was me.
line.jarsLook.2: One jar is labelled "DO NOT". Just that. I've never opened it.
line.jarsLook.3: Clay from the kiln floor, fired in the kiln, storing food for the people who feed the kiln. Very tidy.
line.cartLook.2: Ash goes out, the cart comes back. It's the most reliable thing in Cinderfold.
line.cartLook.3: Someone has painted a small, determined face on the front of it.
line.roomCurtainLook.2: I can smell onions from here. That's Nell's way of calling people.
line.roomCurtainLook.3: The archway is worn smooth at shoulder height from everyone leaning on it to chat.
line.latchLook.2: Brass, older than the door. Mum fitted it the year I was born.
line.latchLook.3: The spring sulks in the cold. So do I, to be fair.
line.soupLook.2: There's always one more bowl in that pot than there are people. Nell plans for strays.
line.soupLook.3: The ladle has a notch where Nell bangs it on the rim to call the night shift.
line.shoesLook.2: The racks hang where the warm air rises. Nobody in Cinderfold has put on cold shoes in years.
line.shoesLook.3: There's a pair of boots at the end that nobody claims. Nell keeps them warm anyway.
line.hearthLook.2: It's fed by a pipe straight from the kiln. No wood, no smoke, just heat that never asks.
line.hearthLook.3: The bricks around it are polished by a hundred winters of hands held out to it.
line.stairsLook.2: Thirty-one steps. Oren counts them out loud on the way up, to annoy the stairs.
line.stairsLook.3: The handrail is warm. Everything that leads to the regulator is warm.
line.gateLook.2: The patchwork curtain is to keep the draught out. It keeps the rest of the world out too.
line.gateLook.3: I've carried parcels through that gate a hundred times. Never anything I didn't want to carry.
line.toRoomLook.2: Back toward the kiln hall and my tent.
line.toRoomLook.3: The way home is always a little warmer than the way out.
line.regulatorLook.2: Mum's maker's mark is stamped on the casing, tiny, as if she didn't want to boast.
line.regulatorLook.3: It ticks, very faintly. Machines aren't supposed to sound thoughtful.
line.gaugeLook.2: The glass is cracked in one corner. Oren says the gauge is fine, the glass just has opinions.
line.gaugeLook.3: Someone painted a little red line on the dial. Above it, in smaller letters: "No."
line.logbookLook.2: His handwriting is perfect, every line. Except today's, which shakes.
line.logbookLook.3: Forty years of readings. The kiln has never missed a day.
line.lanternLook.2: Oren trims the wick every morning before he says a word to anyone.
line.lanternLook.3: The glass is sooted on one side, the side facing the regulator.
line.galleryStairsLook.2: From up here I can hear the soup pot simmering. Or I'm imagining it.
line.galleryStairsLook.3: Thirty-one steps down. Oren doesn't count those. He says going down is just falling slowly.
line.valveLook.2: Someone has scratched an arrow on the wheel. It points both ways.
line.valveLook.3: The pipe behind it is warm to the touch. Something out here still runs.
line.passageLook.2: The bridge above it groans in the wind, politely, like it's clearing its throat.
line.passageLook.3: Beyond it, the ashways go on further than anyone in Cinderfold likes to say.
line.pipesLook.2: A bird's nest is wedged between two pipes. Even out here, something found the warm spot.
line.pipesLook.3: Ash drifts against them like snow against a fence.
line.wayBackLook.2: If I turn around now, nobody would blame me. Except me.
line.wayBackLook.3: I can still see the glow of the gate. Then I can't.
line.heroLook.2: Good boots, Mum's gauntlet, Nell's opinions about my coat. I'm well equipped.
line.heroLook.3: I should get a haircut. I've been saying that since spring.
line.orenLook.2: He's wearing the same scarf he wore when he taught me to read a gauge. It was old then.
line.orenLook.3: He keeps glancing at the regulator the way you'd watch a sleeping animal.
line.nellLook.2: She's humming. Nell hums when she's worried and sings when she isn't.
line.nellLook.3: There's flour on her shutter. There's flour on everything Nell owns.
line.useFails.gauntlet: The gauntlet's for pressure and stubborn springs. This is neither.
line.useFails.notebook: Mum never wrote anything about that. I've checked. Twice.
line.useFails.regulator: I'm not waving the regulator at things. It's cracked enough already.
line.useFails.bread: Bread fixes many things. Not this.
line.useFails.scarf: Tobi would want his scarf used for something heroic. This isn't it.
line.secretTally: Tally marks, cut into the pillar: one for every night someone banked the kiln mouths. The oldest rows are worn almost smooth. The newest ones are mine.
line.secretTallyAgain: I'll owe the pillar a mark for tonight. I don't know who'll cut it.
line.secretChalk: Chalk drawings, low on the wall: a kiln with a smiling face, Nell with a ladle as big as a door, and a tall figure with one enormous glove. Tobi's work. I'm the glove.
line.secretChalkAgain: He's given the kiln eyelashes. I'm not going to tell him kilns don't have eyelashes.
line.secretSign: An old shop sign hangs face-in over the railing. Turned around it reads "NELL'S: SOUP, MENDING, OPINIONS." Someone painted out "mending" years ago. I do the mending now.
line.secretSignAgain: "Opinions" has been repainted at least four times. It's never faded.
line.secretRail: Names scratched into the rail by everyone who ever minded this kiln. Oren's is near the top, very neat. Mine is near the bottom, very crooked.
line.secretRailAgain: There's space under mine. Someone will put their name there one day. I hope I get to meet them.

line.extra-stoker.look: Hollis, the stoker. Shovel in hand, eyebrows singed off years ago.
line.extra-stoker.lookCold: Hollis leans on the shovel, staring at the dark kiln mouths. Nothing to feed.
line.extra-stoker.talk.1: Mind your boots, courier. The ash by the mouths is hotter than it looks.
line.extra-stoker.talk.2: Three shovels to the left mouth, two to the middle. The right one sulks if you overfeed it.
line.extra-stoker.talk.3: You learn a kiln's moods like a mule's. This one's been in a fair mood all week.
line.extra-stoker.talkCold.1: Thirty years I've fed these mouths. Never seen them go dark.
line.extra-stoker.talkCold.2: Don't ask me what to do with my hands now.
line.extra-stoker.chat.1: More coal on the middle mouth!
line.extra-hoist.look: Wren, who works the hoist. Rope burns on both palms, and proud of them.
line.extra-hoist.lookCold: Wren stands under the stopped hoist, one hand still on the rope.
line.extra-hoist.talk.1: The hoist takes the pots up to the drying racks. Pull steady, never jerk it.
line.extra-hoist.talk.2: If that pot ever drops, I want it known it wasn't me.
line.extra-hoist.talk.3: Ask Hollis about the time the rope snapped. Then don't believe a word of it.
line.extra-hoist.talkCold.1: Nothing to haul up if nothing's fired.
line.extra-hoist.talkCold.2: Rope's gone stiff with the cold already.
line.extra-hauler.look: Dace hauls clay from the pile to the kilns. Built like a sack of it, too.
line.extra-hauler.talk.1: Clay from the pile, clay to the mouths. Back and forth till supper.
line.extra-hauler.talk.2: Every sack's the same weight. My back says otherwise.
line.extra-hauler.talk.3: If you're going near the firing house, tell them to keep me some soup.
line.extra-hauler.talkCold.1: No point hauling clay to a cold kiln.
line.extra-hauler.talkCold.2: I'm off to find out what's going on.
line.extra-hauler.chatCold.1: I'm not standing about in this.
line.extra-tally.look: Old Ansel keeps the tally of every load fired. A slate, a stub of chalk, and a long memory.
line.extra-tally.lookCold: Ansel's slate hangs at his side. Nothing to count.
line.extra-tally.talk.1: Forty-two loads this week. Forty-three if that last one doesn't crack.
line.extra-tally.talk.2: I've kept the tally since before you could walk. Chalk's cheaper than paper.
line.extra-tally.talk.3: They say I count in my sleep. Kilns, not sheep.
line.extra-tally.talk.4: Count twice, fire once. That's the rule.
line.extra-tally.talkCold.1: I'll have to write this down. I don't know what to call it.
line.extra-tally.talkCold.2: I'm going to sit somewhere warmer.
line.extra-tally.chat.2: Who fired the left mouth without telling me?
line.extra-runner.look: Pip, the firing house's errand runner. Never walks if running is possible.
line.extra-runner.lookAlarm: Pip has gone very still, pressed against Nell's side.
line.extra-runner.lookCold: Pip sits by the dead hearth with knees pulled up.
line.extra-runner.talk.1: I'm not lost, I'm on an errand! I just forget which.
line.extra-runner.talk.2: Hollis gave me a coin to fetch a cup. I've got the coin, still looking for the cup.
line.extra-runner.talk.3: Is that a gauntlet? Can I touch it? I won't touch it.
line.extra-runner.talkAlarm.1: What was that noise? Nell says it's nothing. Nell's face says something.
line.extra-runner.talkAlarm.2: I'm not scared. I'm just standing here. Next to Nell. On purpose.
line.extra-runner.talkCold.1: Nell says we stay by the hearth. It's not even warm.
line.extra-runner.talkCold.2: Is it broken? The whole kiln?
line.extra-kid.look: Bea, armed with a board from the woodpile and a great deal of confidence.
line.extra-kid.lookAlarm: Bea holds the board up like a real shield, right in front of Nell.
line.extra-kid.lookCold: Bea has put the board down. Sitting on it, by the hearth.
line.extra-kid.talk.1: This is my shield. Nell has a real one. Mine is better because it's mine.
line.extra-kid.talk.2: We're drawing the kiln. Pip draws the fire too big.
line.extra-kid.talk.3: If you're a courier, where's your letters?
line.extra-kid.talkAlarm.1: I'm guarding Nell. Somebody has to.
line.extra-kid.talkAlarm.2: The floor shook. Floors aren't supposed to do that.
line.extra-kid.talkCold.1: My nose is cold. Noses aren't supposed to be cold indoors.
line.extra-kid.talkCold.2: When it's warm again, can I carry the board for you?
intro.1: Beyond the walls the land is ash and wind. Little grows there, and the roads are long and empty.
intro.2: Still, here and there, people hold on: around a fire, a well, a machine that still works. They patch what breaks, and they keep each other going.
intro.3: Cinderfold is one of those places: a village built inside an old kiln, warm for as long as its fire burns.
intro.4: Mara keeps its valves and carries its errands. This morning starts like any other.
line.extra-hauler.leaving.2: Back in a bit. Don't touch my pile.
line.extra-tally.leaving.1: Off to see what the firing house has counted.
line.extra-runner.follow: Where are you going? Can I come?
line.extra-kid.follow: I'm guarding you. Don't mind me.
ui.settingsSample: Nell: "The soup is thin, but it's hot. Sit a moment."
line.orenAfterFight: Are you hurt? That came straight out of the maintenance hatch... and straight for the regulator.
line.maraAfterFight: I'm fine. Mostly. It wanted the regulator, not me.
line.orenGear: Then the road will have more of them. Check your gear before you go. Take my spares: the light coat and the quick harness. Pick what suits you.
battle.strainHelp: Attacks build strain. From 6 to 9 you are hot: attacks deal 2 more damage. At 10 you overload and lose 6 HP.
battle.retry: Mara: "Again. Guard before it hits; watch what it does next."
battle.tut.1: Play Knuckle Drive (click it or press 1). Attacks cost energy: you have 3 a turn.
battle.tut.2: Now Ceramic Guard: block soaks up damage before it reaches you.
battle.tut.3: Look at "Next" above the scavenger: that is what it will do. Then End turn.
battle.tut.4: Kiln Pulse: big damage and block, paid in MP. It builds strain: watch the meter, at 10 you overload.
ui.statHelp.speed: speed 2 or more: one more card in the opening hand; 4 or more: two
